title: Tamsin and the Ghost
premise: Emrys Sterling — born Tamsin Vey, currently living as 'Mara Quill' in a rented flat in Rotterdam — built a life on the documents of three dead people and the silence of one living handler, Aldous Crane. When an encrypted invitation arrives from Crane's address scheduling a meeting for tomorrow at 9 p.m., Emrys goes, and finds Crane dead twelve hours in his chair and a second guest already waiting: a woman claiming to be Tamsin Vey. The impostor carries proof that the whistle-blowing dossier Emrys leaked years ago was itself a controlled burn, designed by three intelligence services to bury a joint black-site program called GHOSTLIGHT. Hunted by an assassin codenamed Lark who kills only with borrowed identities, Emrys must smuggle the real archive past British, Dutch, and American gatekeepers to a journalist's extraction flight leaving Schiphol at dawn — discovering along the way that the impostor is Crane's daughter, raised on stolen fragments of Emrys's erased life. In the end Emrys chooses not to board: they hand the flight to the impostor, walk into the terminal under their own name for the first time in nineteen years, and let the truth travel without them.
about_author: Oscar Yarrow is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing declassified files before turning to fiction, and who still keeps a go-bag out of habit. They write thrillers about people whose names are liabilities, and live somewhere they refuse to specify.

chapters.title: Four Names, One Bag
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. A routine morning in Rotterdam: checking the go-bag, rotating cash, rehearsing the lie of 'Mara Quill' at a neighbor's barbecue. The emotional beat is the exhausting comfort of a life built like a fire escape — everything ready to abandon.

chapters.title: The Invitation
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. An encrypted message arrives from handler Aldous Crane's private key: 'Tomorrow, 21:00, the boathouse. Bring the original.' Emrys knows Crane never uses that phrase. Beat: dread dressed as relief — after six silent years, contact.

chapters.title: What the Bag Weighs
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV, flashback woven through present preparation. We learn what 'the original' is: a physical archive proving GHOSTLIGHT, the tri-national program Emrys exposed and was disowned for exposing. Beat: grief for the self who thought truth would be enough.

chapters.title: The Boathouse
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. At 20:40 Emrys arrives early and finds Crane dead in his chair, twelve hours cold, a glass of whiskey poured for two. On the table: two place settings. Beat: horror sharpening into calculation — someone expected company.

chapters.title: The Other Guest
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. At 21:00 exactly, a woman walks in carrying Emrys's childhood photograph and calls herself Tamsin Vey. She is calm, credentialed, and utterly convincing. Beat: vertigo — meeting your own stolen face.

chapters.title: Lark
chapters.summary: Lark's POV, first appearance. The assassin reviews the boathouse from a canal boat, working from a dossier of borrowed identities, waiting for the principals to lead them to the archive. Beat: professional patience, chillingly intimate knowledge of both women.

chapters.title: Terms of Survival
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The impostor — who gives her name as Wren — proposes alliance: she has Crane's half of the access codes; only together can they open the archive before Lark closes the window. Beat: reluctant truce sealed by mutual hostage-taking of secrets.

chapters.title: Crane's Daughter
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Flashback: raised by Crane on curated stories of the whistle-blower he betrayed, trained to become her. Wren admits she believed she was Tamsin until last month. Beat: identity as inheritance, and inheritance as wound.

chapters.title: The Dutchman
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Contacting an old asset in the Dutch service, Van Dijk, Emrys learns GHOSTLIGHT's files were flagged for destruction by all three governments within seventy-two hours. Beat: the clock becomes a character.

chapters.title: Borrowed Faces
chapters.summary: Lark's POV. Lark murders and briefly 'becomes' a Schiphol cargo officer, seeding the airport net. We see the method: no fingerprints, only other people's lives worn like coats. Beat: elegant, impersonal menace.

chapters.title: The Archive Room
chapters.summary: Emrys and Wren, alternating POV. In a bank vault in Antwerp, the two halves of Crane's cipher open the archive — and reveal the leak Emrys made was sanctioned, a decoy that protected GHOSTLIGHT for a decade. Beat: the floor of Emrys's identity gives way.

chapters.title: Nineteen Years Ago
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV, deep flashback. The night young Tamsin Vey copied the files, the handler who recruited her, the staged death that created 'Emrys.' Beat: mourning the idealist who started this.

chapters.title: Van Dijk's Price
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Van Dijk offers safe passage to the journalist — in exchange for the archive's Dutch section, which implicates his own service. Beat: survival always invoiced; nothing is given.

chapters.title: The American Window
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren works her inherited Crane contacts inside the CIA station in The Hague, trading a favor Crane banked years ago. Beat: using a dead man's credit, feeling him live again through her.

chapters.title: First Blood
chapters.summary: Lark's POV. Lark eliminates Van Dijk's courier and takes his route, meaning the assassin now travels inside the plan. Beat: dread — the enemy is wearing the map.

chapters.title: Two of Everything
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Emrys discovers Wren has been copying the archive onto her own drive. Confrontation in a safehouse: is she heir or thief? Beat: trust fraying into its component lies.

chapters.title: The British Hand
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. A London contact confirms MI6 will deny everything and burn anyone surface-side; the only clean exit is the journalist's dawn flight. Beat: claustrophobia — three governments, zero doors.

chapters.title: Crane's Letters
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Among Crane's effects, letters he never sent: apologies drafted over twenty years, addressed to Tamsin Vey. Wren reads them aloud to Emrys. Beat: posthumous love, arriving too late to be simple.

chapters.title: Checkpoint
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Crossing from Belgium back into the Netherlands, the pair passes a checkpoint where Lark — wearing a border officer's identity — looks directly at Emrys and lets them through. Beat: terror of being spared, because you're being saved for something.

chapters.title: The Journalist
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Meeting Ilsa Brandt, the investigative journalist running the extraction, Emrys must convince her the story is bigger than one leak: it's a decade of manufactured history. Beat: handing your life's work to a stranger's judgment.

chapters.title: Wren's Confession
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren reveals Crane didn't just raise her on Emrys's story — he commissioned her creation, growing a replacement whistle-blower in case the original broke. Beat: pity and fury braided together.

chapters.title: Safehouse Siege
chapters.summary: Action chapter, alternating POV. Lark hits the safehouse with a four-person team wearing police identities. Escape through adjoining canal houses; a friendly boatman dies covering them. Beat: the cost of survival made flesh.

chapters.title: The Boatman's Name
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Emrys insists on learning the dead man's real name and notifying his daughter — breaking every rule of a life built on anonymity. Beat: reclamation of consequence.

chapters.title: GHOSTLIGHT, Opened
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Full decryption: the program ran rendition flights through civilian airlines, and the 'leak' Emrys made was timed to discredit a genuine internal objector who was then disappeared. Beat: rage with nowhere to put it.

chapters.title: The Disappeared Man
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. The objector — Daniel Okonkwo — may still be alive in a detention pipeline. Emrys faces a choice: flight at dawn, or hours spent finding him. Beat: conscience versus arithmetic.

chapters.title: Splitting the Night
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Wren argues for the flight; Emrys refuses to leave Okonkwo in the machine. They split tasks: Wren to Brandt and the flight, Emrys into the detention system with forged credentials. Beat: partnership becoming something like faith.

chapters.title: Inside the Pipeline
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Using a dead guard's identity, Emrys reaches Okonkwo's holding facility outside Amsterdam and finds him sedated but alive, scheduled for transfer at 04:00. Beat: hope as a tactical liability.

chapters.title: Lark's Contract
chapters.summary: Lark's POV. Lark's employers change the contract: not the archive anymore — the witnesses. Lark feels the first hairline crack in professional detachment, remembering a target once spared. Beat: the instrument developing a pulse.

chapters.title: Extraction, Interrupted
chapters.summary: Action, alternating POV. Emrys pulls Okonkwo out during a shift change as Lark closes in; a chase through freight yards ends with Emrys cornered — and Lark lowering the weapon, demanding to hear the file read aloud. Beat: the hunter defecting to the evidence.

chapters.title: Reading Aloud
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. In a rail yard office at 03:00, Emrys reads the GHOSTLIGHT summary to Lark, whose brother was one of the rendered. Beat: testimony as the only weapon left.

chapters.title: Dawn Approaches
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. At Schiphol, Brandt's charter is held by a customs flag placed from Washington. Wren spends Crane's last favor — a call to a deputy director — knowing it exposes her permanently. Beat: spending your inheritance to buy the truth an hour.

chapters.title: The Runway Decision
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Emrys, Okonkwo, and Lark race toward the airfield as the flag lifts. Emrys realizes any face on that plane becomes a lifelong target — including Okonkwo's, including Wren's. Beat: the price of survival itemized.

chapters.title: Handover
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. At the fence line, Emrys makes the choice: Wren boards with the archive and Okonkwo, carrying the story and the name Tamsin Vey forward; Emrys stays behind as the visible decoy. Beat: giving away your own ghost.

chapters.title: Terminal Light
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Aboard the climbing charter at sunrise, Wren watches the terminal and understands she is now the keeper of two lives. Beat: inheritance finally accepted, trembling.

chapters.title: Walking In
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Emrys walks into Schiphol's main terminal, buys coffee under their own name, and waits — deliberately visible — while the plane clears airspace. Beat: terror transfigured into freedom.

chapters.title: Lark's Report
chapters.summary: Lark's POV. Lark files a report stating the principal escaped abroad, untraceable — the first lie of Lark's career — and burns the contract file. Beat: an instrument choosing its own note.

chapters.title: Three Governments, One Morning
chapters.summary: Multi-POV montage. London, The Hague, and Washington absorb the publication: denials drafted, careers ended, GHOSTLIGHT's remnants dismantled in haste. Beat: the machinery grinding against daylight and losing.

chapters.title: Tamsin Vey, Alive
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Weeks later, Emrys legally restores the birth name in a Rotterdam municipal office — the paperwork banal, the moment enormous. Beat: identity reclaimed as an act, not a document.

chapters.title: The Letter
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. A letter arrives from Wren, postmarked wherever the story landed: Crane's unsent letters enclosed, plus one new page of her own. Beat: forgiveness begun across an ocean.

chapters.title: One Name, No Bag
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV, closing. Emrys unpacks the go-bag at last, hangs the coat up properly, and answers the door to a visitor — Lark, unarmed, asking how to testify. Beat: survival's true price paid, and worth it.
